name: CMSIS-DSP
listed_description: Arm library of over 60 DSP functions for several data types, optimized for the SIMD instruction sets on Cortex-M4, M7, M33 and M35P.
claim_text: Library of over 60 functions optimized for the SIMD instruction sets of Cortex-M4, M7, M33 and M35P; no timings given.
guessed_baseline: plain C loops and libm routines on Cortex-M, or CMSIS-DSP reference C build without SIMD
found_in: book: Bare-Metal Embedded C Programming (2025), ch. 6, section Key components of CMSIS

name: CMSIS-NN
listed_description: Arm collection of efficient neural network kernels tuned for speed and small memory footprint on Cortex-M cores.
claim_text: Efficient neural network kernels optimized to maximize performance and minimize memory footprint on Cortex-M cores; no numbers given.
found_in: book: Bare-Metal Embedded C Programming (2025), ch. 6, section Key components of CMSIS

name: STM32 Low Layer (LL) driver library
listed_description: STMicroelectronics leaner, expert-oriented register-level driver layer for STM32, shipped beside HAL in the STM32Cube MCU package.
claim_text: LL is a leaner alternative to HAL, offering a faster approach closer to the hardware; HAL is slightly slower because of abstraction layers.
found_in: book: Bare-Metal Embedded C Programming (2025), ch. 2, sections Different types of firmware development and LL

name: Direct register access in bare-metal C (versus HAL and LL)
listed_description: Configure GPIO and other peripherals by writing memory-mapped registers directly through volatile pointers or CMSIS-style structs, with no vendor library in between.
listed_license: MIT (per companion repository page, not the book)
claim_text: Performance very high, as it allows direct and optimized hardware manipulation; assembly rated highest. Qualitative only.
book_benchmark: No timing measured. Book compares code size and style of the same GPIO pin setup in HAL, LL, bare-metal C and assembly on STM32F411 (Cortex-M4); builds shown use arm-none-eabi-gcc with -O0 in the IDE debug profile.
guessed_baseline: STM32 HAL GPIO driver calls (HAL_GPIO_Init and friends)
found_in: book: Bare-Metal Embedded C Programming (2025), ch. 2, section Different types of firmware development; ch. 6, section Evaluating the structure-based register access method

name: GPIO BSRR single-write set/reset (versus ODR read-modify-write)
listed_description: Drive an STM32 output pin through the bit set/reset register, one atomic write that cannot be disturbed by interrupts, instead of read-modify-write on the output data register.
listed_license: MIT (per companion repository page, not the book)
claim_text: BSRR provides atomic bitwise set or reset of individual pins, so interrupts cannot disrupt the operation; no speed figure.
found_in: book: Bare-Metal Embedded C Programming (2025), ch. 7, sections GPIO bit-set/reset register and GPIO output driver using the BSRR
